description: #177 real-machine gap (surfaced this round, never in sandbox): stack.sh shadowed the non-placed .env* only for `next` apps. The BE (mootech-be) is a `node`/NestJS app that loads ONLY .env (verified: no envFilePath in any ConfigModule.forRoot, no dotenv dep — nestjs/config default), so its prod .env.dev.local / .env.prod.local / .env.local (holding prod DB pooler + api.line.me + 8x8.com + the Supabase service-role key) were NEVER shadowed and stayed ACTIVE on disk. The #177 whole-active-set guard + #184 provider scan correctly REFUSED and the up rolled back fail-closed — but the stack could not come up. Fix (chosen over making the guard node-aware, which would just narrow the question so it passes): run shadow_others for EVERY app, not just next — so only the neutralized .env stays active (a real reduction of what's reachable, not a narrower guard) + defense-in-depth (prod service-role moved aside during test). ensure_local_ignore still runs BEFORE shadow_others for the BE dir (#119 window stays closed — verified the 3 shadowed BE files are git check-ignore'd). Why sandbox missed it: the #177/#178 sandbox had no node app carrying multiple prod .env.*.local files — clean-state tests can't answer dirty-state questions (2nd instance of that lesson this week). Teeth (real machine): up now shadows all 3 BE prod files + keeps .env.example (is_committed_template covers BE), guard passes, BE boots; migration — new restore recovers a shadowed state (4 BE files byte-identical to prod) AND an OLD never-shadowed state (restores .env from backup, leaves the untouched prod files, no phantom un-shadow); the earlier guard-fail rollback exercised the mid-run EXIT trap on the real machine. gate_layer=infra/shell.
